subject: Career
title: Dunbar's Number: Your Social Limit
description: A 60-second lesson on Dunbar's Number: Your Social Limit.

hook.text: You have 1,200 LinkedIn connections. But your brain can only maintain about 150 real relationships.

buildup.text: Anthropologist Robin Dunbar found a correlation between brain size and social group size.

discovery.text: 150 is the max for meaningful relationships. Within that: 5 close, 15 good, 50 friends, 150 acquaintances.

twist.text: Social media inflates our perceived network. But connection isn't relationship.

climax.text: Quality over quantity isn't just a cliché. It's a neurological constraint.

punchline.text: Your brain has a limit. Fill those 150 slots wisely.

details.summary: Anthropologist Robin Dunbar proposed that humans can maintain meaningful relationships with approximately one hundred fifty people, constrained by cognitive limits. Beyond this number, relationships become superficial acquaintances.
details.whyItMatters: Trying to network with everyone leads to shallow connections with no one. Dunbar's number helps you prioritize depth over breadth in professional relationship building.
takeaways: The one-hundred-fifty limit includes personal and professional contacts
Inner circles of fifteen and five people carry the deepest trust
Technology extends reach but does not expand cognitive relationship limits

faq.question: Does Dunbar's number mean you should limit your LinkedIn connections?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. LinkedIn connections beyond one hundred fifty serve as weak ties that provide information access and bridging capital. The limit applies to relationships you actively maintain and invest in, not to the total number of digital contacts.

faq.question: How should Dunbar's number inform your networking strategy?
faq.answer: Prioritize your inner fifteen relationships with regular investment, maintain your one-hundred-fifty with periodic touchpoints, and use digital tools to stay loosely connected with the broader network. Quality always trumps quantity in networking.
